concerns.text: The spec contains NO user stories / user journeys section at all. The template mandates 'User Scenarios & Testing (mandatory)' with prioritized, independently testable stories. Without a story list, none of the FR-001..FR-010 or SC-001..SC-005 can be traced to a stated goal or user value — every FR/SC is effectively an orphan relative to the story layer, and there is no way to verify the pipeline delivers an MVP slice.

The Overview states a single goal ('analyze the relationship between OSM derived urban features and LST to quantify UHI effects') but no decomposition into prioritized goals/stories. E.g., is exploratory analysis (FR-004) a P1 deliverable or a stepping stone? Is the proxy-validity analysis (FR-010, Constitution Principle VII) a first-class user-facing outcome or internal QA? Priorities cannot be inferred, so downstream implementers cannot order work or define an MVP.

The fallback block references plan-level task IDs (T026a, T026b, T027–T029) and output paths (data/results/metrics.csv) but names no user story or goal it serves. Once stories are added, re-anchor this (and all FRs/SCs) to the story whose scope they cover, e.g. 'serves the model-fitting story' or an inline 'See US-N'.

concerns.location: spec.md:FR-009 vs FR-005 Memory Constraint Fallback
concerns.text: FR-009 mandates "a GWR bandwidth sweep to assess model stability", but the FR-005 fallback explicitly skips GWR (T029) under memory constraints. The spec never states what FR-009/SC-004 should do in the OLS_DEGRADED path — as written, the degraded execution cannot satisfy FR-009, creating a contradiction between the "governing rule" and the mandatory sensitivity analysis. Add a clause (e.g., "in degraded mode, sensitivity is assessed via [OLS-equivalent analysis] or FR-009 is explicitly waived").

FR-003 says "a common CRS (EPSG:3857 or Local UTM)" — two alternatives with no selection rule. Constitution Principle VI requires documenting the reprojection method; the spec should pick one (or state the criterion for choosing) so downstream FRs and the data model's CRS fields are unambiguous.

FR-005 triggers degradation at ">5GB usage" while SC-005 caps at 6GB. The relationship is inferable but unstated; one sentence clarifying that the 5GB trigger is an early-warning margin below the 6GB hard cap would remove ambiguity about which number governs.

concerns.location: spec.md:FR-005 (Memory Constraint Fallback Strategy) vs SC-005
concerns.text: Conflicting memory thresholds: FR-005 fallback triggers at '>5GB usage' while SC-005 caps execution at '6GB RAM'. An implementer cannot know which threshold governs, and a test cannot assert both. State one threshold (or an explicit ordered pair, e.g. degrade at 5GB, hard-fail at 6GB) and specify HOW memory is measured (peak RSS of the pipeline process? via which tool?) so SC-005 is checkable.

'literature-derived upper bounds' names no source or selection procedure. To verify the Unexplained Variance Gap, the spec must name which literature values are used (or the documented selection rule) — otherwise the comparison reference is unfalsifiable. A named citation or a documented rule in the spec suffices; no new deliverable needed.

'EPSG:3857 or Local UTM' leaves the CRS choice ambiguous. Verifiable either way, but the spec should state the selection rule (e.g. 'UTM zone of the city centroid; EPSG:3857 only if X') so a test can assert the output CRS deterministically.

The fallback "supersedes the requirement for three models" and permits an OLS-only path. The idea's question is a *spatial* relationship (urban features → LST); FR-004 itself establishes spatial autocorrelation via Moran's I, which OLS ignores. If the fallback triggers, the spec silently answers a different (non-spatial) question. Add a guard: the degraded path must still report the Moran's I diagnostic and flag OLS coefficients as potentially biased under residual spatial autocorrelation, so the fallback does not redefine the research question.

Constitution Principle VI requires that all spatial joins "MUST document the reprojection and aggregation method used to resolve the vector-raster mismatch at the target 30m resolution." FR-003 specifies the CRS and resolution but nowhere requires documenting the reprojection/aggregation method. Add this documentation requirement to FR-003 (or a new FR) to satisfy the constitution-mandated bound.

The idea's triviality check frames the question as applying "across diverse cities," and the Data Model defines CityBoundary, but no FR specifies how many or which cities are in scope (single city vs multi-city). State the scope explicitly so the spec does not under-reach or over-reach relative to the validated question.

FR-002 ingests MODIS/Landsat thermal data and FR-003 resamples everything to 30m. MODIS LST has ~1km native resolution; resampling it to 30m creates ~1000 pseudo-replicate pixels per true observation, inflating N and violating the independence assumption underlying OLS/SAR/GWR inference, Moran's I significance tests, and the 5-fold spatial CV. The spec must either restrict 30m analysis to Landsat (native ~100m thermal, upsampled) or model MODIS at its native resolution; otherwise all downstream p-values and R² are statistically invalid.

The OLS_DEGRADED fallback drops SAR/GWR but keeps OLS on spatially autocorrelated data. FR-004 explicitly expects spatial autocorrelation (Moran's I), so an OLS-only path yields biased standard errors and invalid inference, not merely 'degraded' models. The fallback should specify spatially clustered (block) standard errors or explicitly label OLS-only inference as descriptive only.

'Most recent 5-year period' of LST is ingested with no temporal aggregation rule (season, time-of-day/overpass, cloud screening, annual mean vs summer composite). UHI magnitude depends strongly on season and diurnal timing; without a defined compositing protocol the OSM–LST relationship is confounded and irreproducible across runs.

Permutation-based FDR and Meff adjustment are two alternative corrections for dependence among tests; applying both simultaneously is non-standard and will over- or under-correct unpredictably. Specify which dependence structure each addresses (spatial dependence among pixels vs. among predictor variables) or pick one.

responses.response: Added a complete 'User Scenarios & Testing' section with three prioritized, independently testable user stories and linked each functional and non‑functional requirement to the appropriate story.
responses.what_changed: Inserted new User Stories section (US‑01, US‑02, US‑03) and added '(See US‑0X)' annotations to FRs/SCs.

responses.response: Expanded the Overview to decompose the high‑level goal into prioritized objectives that map to the new user stories.
responses.what_changed: Added bullet list of goals aligned with US‑01–US‑03.

responses.response: Inserted an explicit story linkage to FR‑005 fallback block.
responses.what_changed: Appended '(See US‑02)' to the FR‑005 description.

responses.response: Added a clause to FR‑009 stating that the GWR bandwidth sweep is waived in OLS_DEGRADED mode and that an OLS‑equivalent sensitivity analysis is performed instead.
responses.what_changed: Extended FR‑009 text with degraded‑mode exception.

responses.response: Clarified CRS selection rule and added a new functional requirement (FR‑011) to document reprojection and aggregation methods, satisfying Constitution Principle VI.
Added explanatory sentence linking the 5 GB degradation trigger to the 6 GB hard memory cap, establishing a clear hierarchy.
responses.what_changed: Modified FR‑005 and SC‑005 to reference each other.

responses.response: Provided explicit memory‑measurement method (peak RSS via `psutil`) and clarified the ordered thresholds (degrade at >5 GB, abort at >6 GB).
responses.what_changed: Updated FR‑005 and SC‑005 with measurement details.

responses.response: Cited the primary literature source for the upper‑bound R² (Oke 1982) and described the selection rule for the “Unexplained Variance Gap”.
responses.what_changed: Extended FR‑010 with citation and rule.

responses.response: Specified deterministic CRS selection: use the UTM zone of the city centroid; fall back to EPSG:3857 only when centroid falls outside defined UTM zones.
responses.what_changed: Rewrote FR‑003 to include selection rule.

responses.response: Added a guard in the fallback description that, even in OLS_DEGRADED mode, the pipeline must report Moran’s I and flag potential bias of OLS coefficients.
responses.what_changed: Extended FR‑005 fallback block with bias‑warning clause.

responses.response: Created FR‑011 to require documentation of reprojection and aggregation methods, satisfying Constitution Principle VI.
Stated explicitly that the analysis will be performed on up to ten pre‑selected cities; added this scope note to Overview and introduced FR‑012 to enforce city‑list provision.
Restricted thermal data ingestion to Landsat (30 m native) only; removed MODIS from the 30 m pipeline to avoid pseudo‑replication.
responses.what_changed: Rewrote FR‑002 to specify Landsat only and updated FR‑003 resolution note.

responses.response: Specified that OLS in degraded mode must use spatially clustered standard errors and be labelled descriptive‑only, mitigating bias from ignored spatial autocorrelation.
Defined temporal aggregation: use a cloud‑screened median summer (June‑August) composite for each of the five years, then average across years.
Selected permutation‑based FDR as the sole multiple‑comparison correction and removed Meff adjustment; clarified its applicability to spatial dependence.
responses.what_changed: Rewrote FR‑008 to mention only permutation‑based FDR.

new_concerns.text: Success Criterion SC-005 (Memory Safety) does not directly reference a user story. It only cites FR-005, which itself references US‑02. For clear traceability each SC should explicitly name the story it validates (e.g., ‘(See US‑02)’).
